chunks: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while wearing a khazz coat and a khazz pallium. He looked at me, so I said: 'May I be your ransom! Upon me is a khazz coat and a khazz pallium — what do you say about it?' He said: 'And what is the problem with khazz?' I said: 'And its warp is silk (ibraysam).' He said: 'And what is the problem with silk? For indeed al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was struck down while upon him was a khazz coat.'

Then he said: 'Indeed, when Abdullah ibn Abbas — when Amir al-Mu'mineen (peace be upon him) sent him to the Khawarij to confront them — he wore the best of his garments, perfumed himself with the best of his perfumes, and rode the best of his mounts. Then he went out and confronted them. They said: O Ibn Abbas! Even though you are the best of the people, you have come to us in the garments of tyrants and their mounts!'
So he recited to them this verse: 'Say: Who has forbidden the adornments of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions?'
So wear (fine garments) and beautify yourself, for Allah is Beautiful and He loves beauty — but let it be from the permissible.

key_terms.إِبْرِيسَم: Ibraysam — pure silk threads; using pure silk warp in khazz raised questions about permissibility
key_terms.الْجَبَابِرَة: Al-Jababira — tyrants or oppressors; the Khawarij accused Ibn Abbas of dressing like rulers
key_terms.جَمِيلٌ: Jamil — Beautiful; Allah's attribute of beauty used to justify wearing beautiful garments
key_terms.خَزّ: Khazz — a fabric woven from a combination of silk and wool, widely worn in early Islamic society; its permissibility was a major fiqh debate
key_terms.طَيْلَسَان: Tayalisan — a large pallium or shawl worn over the shoulders, common in classical Islamic dress

ai.seo_question: Is wearing khazz (silk-wool fabric) permissible in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a jurisprudential question about wearing khazz garments — a type of fabric woven from silk and wool. The narrator Yusuf ibn Ibrahim came to the Imam wearing such clothing and asked about its permissibility, particularly since its warp threads were pure silk. The Imam permitted it emphatically, citing that Imam al-Husayn (AS) himself wore khazz at his martyrdom. The hadith then preserves a second teaching: when Ibn Abbas was sent by Imam Ali (AS) to debate the Khawarij, he dressed in his finest attire, and when challenged, responded by reciting Quran 7:32, declaring that Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty — with the condition that it come from permissible (halal) means.
